source.title: Open problems in commutative ring theory

accepted.question_text: Let R be a Prüfer ring, where a Prüfer ring is one in which every finitely generated regular ideal is invertible. Is the finitistic projective dimension fp.dim(R), defined as the supremum of proj.dim_R(M) over modules M in mod R having finite projective dimension, always at most 1?
accepted.context_brief: Prüfer rings and finitistic projective dimension

evidence.quote: Problem 1a. Let R be a Prüfer ring. Is fp.dim R <= 1?

accepted.question_text: Let R be a total ring of quotients. Is its finitistic projective dimension fp.dim(R) equal to 0?

evidence.quote: Problem 1b. Let R be a total ring of quotients. Is fp.dim R = 0?

accepted.question_text: If R is a Gaussian ring, meaning c(fg) = c(f)c(g) for all f,g in R[x], must the weak global dimension w.dim(R) belong to the set {0, 1, infinity}?
accepted.context_brief: Weak global dimension of Gaussian rings

evidence.quote: Problem 2a. If R is a Gaussian ring, then is w.dim R = 0, 1, or infinity?

accepted.question_text: If R is a total ring of quotients, must the weak global dimension w.dim(R) belong to the set {0, 1, infinity}?
accepted.context_brief: Weak global dimension of total quotient rings

evidence.quote: Problem 2b. If R is a total ring of quotients, is w.dim R = 0, 1, or infinity?

accepted.question_text: What values can the weak global dimension w.dim(R) take when R is a Prüfer ring?
accepted.context_brief: Weak global dimension of Prüfer rings

evidence.quote: Problem 2c. What are the values of w.dim R when R is a Prüfer ring?

accepted.question_text: If D is a one-dimensional coherent domain, is the integral closure of D in its field of quotients necessarily a Prüfer domain?

evidence.quote: Problem 3. Is the integral closure of a one dimensional coherent domain in its field of quotients a Prüfer domain?

accepted.question_text: Let R be a G-GCD ring and G a finitely generated abelian group. Do the finite conductor property and the quasi-coherent property ascend from R to the group ring RG?
accepted.context_brief: Ascent of finite conductor and quasi-coherent properties

evidence.quote: Problem 4a. Assume that R is a G-GCD ring and G is a finitely generated abelian group. Do the finite conductor and the quasi coherent properties ascend from R to RG?

accepted.question_text: Are the finite conductor property and the quasi-coherent property distinct properties for commutative rings?

evidence.quote: Problem 4b. Are the finite conductor and quasi coherent properties for rings distinct?

accepted.question_text: Let R be a commutative ring and G an abelian group such that the order of every element of G is invertible in R. Is there a formula relating the global dimension of the group ring RG to the global dimension of R together with some invariant of G?

evidence.quote: Problem 5a. Is there a similar formula that relates the global dimension of RG to the global dimension of R in combination with some invariant of the group G?

accepted.question_text: Find characterizations of those group rings that are semisimple and of those that are hereditary.

evidence.quote: Problem 5b. Find characterizations of semisimple and hereditary group rings.

accepted.question_text: For a commutative ring R and an abelian group G, determine when the group ring RG is Cohen-Macaulay and when it is Gorenstein in the non-Noetherian sense developed in the cited literature.
accepted.context_brief: Non-Noetherian Cohen-Macaulay and Gorenstein group rings

evidence.quote: The questions of when a group ring RG, where R is a commutative ring and G is an abelian group, is Cohen-Macaulay or Gorenstein have yet to be investigated.

accepted.question_text: Is there a non-Noetherian characterization of local complete intersection rings such that coherent local Gorenstein rings are complete intersections and coherent local complete intersection rings are Cohen-Macaulay?

evidence.quote: Is there a non-Noetherian characterization of local complete intersection rings such that (coherent) local Gorenstein rings are complete intersections, and such that (coherent) local complete intersection rings are Cohen-Macaulay?

accepted.question_text: If a Noetherian local ring is weakly quasi-complete, must it be quasi-complete?

evidence.quote: Problem 8a. Is a weakly quasi-complete ring quasi-complete?

accepted.question_text: Let k be a field and R = k[X1,...,Xn]_(X1,...,Xn) with n >= 2. Is R weakly quasi-complete, or even quasi-complete?

evidence.quote: Problem 8b. Let k be a field and R = k[X1,...,Xn]_(X1,...,Xn), n >= 2. Is R (weakly) quasi-complete?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an integrally closed reduced ring R such that for every maximal ideal M, the localization R_M is an integrally closed McCoy ring, while R itself is not a McCoy ring and is not locally a domain?
accepted.context_brief: McCoy rings and integrally closed polynomial extensions

evidence.quote: Does there exist an integrally closed reduced ring R such that R_M is an integrally closed McCoy ring for each maximal ideal M, but R is not a McCoy ring and it is not locally a domain?

accepted.question_text: Do there exist reduced rings that satisfy both the annihilator condition (a.c.) and the condition (A_n) for some n >= 2, but are nevertheless not McCoy rings?

evidence.quote: Do there exist reduced rings that have both (a.c.) and (A_n) for some n >= 2 that are not McCoy rings?

accepted.question_text: Let P be a nonzero prime ideal of a Prüfer domain R. Characterize when, for every Prüfer domain T with T contained in R and having the same quotient field as R, the contracted prime P ∩ T is a divisorial prime of T.
accepted.context_brief: Divisorial primes under contraction to Prüfer subrings

evidence.quote: Problem 11a. Characterize when P (and R) is such that P∩T is a divisorial prime of T for each Prüfer domain T ⊆ R with the same quotient field as R.

accepted.question_text: Let P be a nonzero prime ideal of a Prüfer domain R. Characterize when there is no Prüfer domain T contained in R, with the same quotient field as R, such that the contracted prime P ∩ T is a divisorial prime of T.
accepted.context_brief: Failure of divisorial contraction in Prüfer subrings

evidence.quote: Problem 11b. Characterize when P (and R) is such that there is no Prüfer domain T ⊆ R with the same quotient field as R such that P∩T is a divisorial prime of T.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a Prüfer domain R with a nonzero prime P and a countably infinite chain of overrings R = R0 ⊂ R1 ⊂ R2 ⊂ ... ⊂ R_P such that for every n >= 0, PR_{2n} is divisorial in R_{2n} while PR_{2n+1} is not divisorial in R_{2n+1}? If such a chain exists, is P S divisorial or non-divisorial in S = union of the R_m inside R_P?
accepted.context_brief: Alternating divisorial behavior along Prüfer overrings

evidence.quote: Problem 12a. Does there exist a Prüfer domain R with a nonzero prime P such that there is a countably infinite chain of overrings R = R0 ⊂ R1 ⊂ R2 ⊂ ... ⊂ R_P where for all n >= 0, PR_{2n} is a divisorial ideal of R_{2n} and PR_{2n+1} is an ideal of R_{2n+1} that is not divisorial? If such a chain exists, is PS divisorial or not divisorial as an ideal of S?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a Prüfer domain R with a nonzero prime P and a countably infinite chain of underrings R = R0 ⊃ R1 ⊃ R2 ⊃ ... ⊃ T, all with the same quotient field, such that for every n >= 0, P ∩ R_{2n} is divisorial in R_{2n} while P ∩ R_{2n+1} is not divisorial in R_{2n+1}? If such a chain exists, is P ∩ T divisorial or non-divisorial in T?
accepted.context_brief: Alternating divisorial behavior along Prüfer underrings

evidence.quote: Problem 12b. Does there exist a Prüfer domain R with a nonzero prime P such that there is a countably infinite chain of underrings R = R0 ⊃ R1 ⊃ R2 ⊃ ... ⊃ T with T having the same quotient field as R where for all n >= 0, P∩R_{2n} is a divisorial ideal of R_{2n} and P∩R_{2n+1} is not a divisorial ideal of R_{2n+1}? If such a chain exists, is P∩T divisorial or not divisorial as an ideal of T?

accepted.question_text: If R_P and R/P are straight domains, does it follow that the pullback ring R + P R_P is also a straight domain?

evidence.quote: Problem 13a. If R_P and R/P are straight domains does this imply that R + PR_P is a straight domain?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a straight domain that is not locally divided?
accepted.context_brief: Straight domains versus locally divided domains

evidence.quote: Problem 13b. Does there exist a straight domain which is not locally divided?

accepted.question_text: For an integral domain D, is the Krull dimension of the ring Int(D) of integer-valued polynomials always bounded above by the dimension of D[X], as conjectured by the source after noting that dim(Int(D)) >= dim(D[X]) - 1?
accepted.context_brief: Dimension of rings of integer-valued polynomials

evidence.quote: The question of an upper bound remains open: It is conjectured to be equal to dim(D[X]).

accepted.question_text: For a one-dimensional local Noetherian domain D with finite residue field, determine necessary and sufficient conditions for Int(D) to satisfy the almost strong Skolem property.

evidence.quote: When does Int(D) satisfy the almost strong Skolem property?

accepted.question_text: Besides the known families coming from iterates of nonconstant polynomials in Z[X], determine other self-ordered integer sequences, where a sequence (a_n) is self-ordered when for all positive integers m,n one has product_{k=0}^{n-1}(a_n-a_k) dividing product_{k=0}^{n-1}(a_m-a_k).

evidence.quote: The question is: Are there any other natural self ordered sequences neither obtained by a dynamical construction nor by an affine map applied to the three previous examples?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an infinite subset E of Z whose Bhargava factorial sequence (n!_E) is not ultimately strictly increasing?

evidence.quote: Are there subsets E of Z such that the sequence of Bhargava’s factorials (n!_E) is not ultimately strictly increasing?

accepted.question_text: For which infinite subsets E of Z is the constant e_E = sum_{n>=0} 1/(n!_E), formed from the Bhargava factorials of E, a transcendental number?

evidence.quote: For which infinite subset E is e_E a transcendental number?

accepted.question_text: For an arbitrary integral domain D, is Int(D) always a flat D-module?

evidence.quote: Problem 19a. Is Int(D) a flat D-module for any domain D?

accepted.question_text: For an arbitrary integral domain D, is Int(D) always a free D-module?

evidence.quote: Problem 19b. Is Int(D) a free D-module for any domain D?

accepted.question_text: For an integral domain D, is the canonical D-algebra homomorphism Int(D) tensor_D n -> Int(D^n) always injective, and is it always surjective?

evidence.quote: Is this canonical morphism always injective? surjective?

accepted.question_text: For an integral domain D, does Int(D) always admit a unique structure of a D-D-biring for which the inclusion D[X] -> Int(D) is a homomorphism of D-D-birings?

evidence.quote: Problem 21. Let D be an integral domain. Does Int(D) always have a unique structure of a D-D-biring such that the inclusion D[X] -> Int(D) is a homomorphism of D-D-birings?

accepted.question_text: If D ⊆ A is an extension of domains and Int(D) ⊆ Int(A), does it follow that the extension D ⊆ A is almost polynomially complete, meaning Int(D^n) ⊆ Int(A^n) for all positive integers n?

evidence.quote: If Int(D) ⊆ Int(A), does it follow that the extension D ⊆ A is almost polynomially complete?

accepted.question_text: Let K be a number field with ring of integers O_K, and let Int_n(O_K) be the O_K-module of integer-valued polynomials of degree at most n. Prove or disprove that the natural density of the set of n for which Int_n(O_K) is free exists, is rational, and is at least 1/Card(Pólya group(O_K)); then compute that density.
accepted.context_brief: Density of free truncations of Int(O_K)

evidence.quote: Prove or disprove the following conjecture: δ(Int(O_K)) exists, is rational, and is at least 1/Card(Pólya group(O_K)). Then compute δ(Int(O_K)).

accepted.question_text: Let E be the set of values of a second-order recursive integer sequence u_{n+1} = a u_n + b u_{n-1} with initial values u_0,u_1. Compute a regular basis of the Z-module Int(E;Z), meaning a basis whose n-th term has degree n.
accepted.context_brief: Regular bases for recursive integer-valued polynomial rings

evidence.quote: Problem 24a. Compute a regular basis (that is, a basis with n-th term of degree n) of the Z-module Int(E;Z).

accepted.question_text: For the same recursive set E, compute the characteristic sequence of Int(E;Z) with respect to each prime p, namely the sequence of p-adic valuations of the leading-coefficient fractional ideals in each degree.

evidence.quote: Problem 24b. Compute the characteristic sequence of Int(E;Z) with respect to each prime p, that is, the sequence φ_p(n), where φ_p(n) is the p-adic valuation of the fractional ideal consisting of 0 and the leading coefficients of elements of Int(E;Z) of degree no more than n.

accepted.question_text: For the same recursive set E, determine the asymptotic behavior of the characteristic sequence by computing the limit of φ(n)/n, where φ(n) is the p-adic valuation sequence described in the source.

evidence.quote: Problem 24c. Determine the asymptotic behavior of this sequence, that is, compute the limit lim_{n→∞} φ(n)/n.

accepted.question_text: Compute a regular basis of Int_Q(M_n(Z)), the ring of rational-coefficient polynomials that are integer-valued on n x n integer matrices.
accepted.context_brief: Regular bases for matrix-valued integer-valued polynomial rings

evidence.quote: Problem 25a. Compute a regular basis of Int_Q(M_n(Z)).

accepted.question_text: Compute the characteristic sequence of Int_Q(M_n(Z)) with respect to each prime p.

evidence.quote: Problem 25b. Compute its characteristic sequence with respect to each prime p.

accepted.question_text: Determine the asymptotic behavior of the characteristic sequence of Int_Q(M_n(Z)).

evidence.quote: Problem 25c. Determine the asymptotic behavior of this sequence.

accepted.question_text: Let D be an integral domain and A a torsion-free D-algebra that is finitely generated as a D-module. Characterize those algebras A for which Int_K(A) equals the intersection over a in A of the pullback rings D[X] + μ_a(X)K[X], where μ_a(X) is the minimal polynomial of a over D.

evidence.quote: For which algebras A as above does this inclusion become an equality?

accepted.question_text: Give an example of a D-algebra A for which Int(A), the set of B[X]-polynomials that map A to itself, is not a ring, possibly after relaxing some of the standing hypotheses on A.
accepted.context_brief: When Int(A) fails to be a ring

evidence.quote: Problem 27a. Give an example of a D-algebra A such that Int(A) is not a ring (possibly relaxing some of the conditions on A, for instance that A is finitely generated as a D-module).

accepted.question_text: Assume D has finite residue rings. Is Int(A) always a ring for every torsion-free D-algebra A of the kind considered in the source, or can one construct a counterexample?

evidence.quote: Problem 27b. Prove this conjecture or give a counterexample in this case.

accepted.question_text: Determine when the integral closure of Int_K(A) is a Prüfer domain.
accepted.context_brief: Prüfer criteria for integral closures of Int_K(A)

evidence.quote: Determine when this integral closure is Prüfer.

accepted.question_text: Describe the integrally closed rings lying between a two-dimensional Noetherian domain D and its quotient field F.

evidence.quote: Describe the integrally closed rings between a two-dimensional Noetherian domain and its quotient field.

accepted.question_text: If I is an n-absorbing ideal of a ring R, must I also be strongly n-absorbing?

evidence.quote: Problem 30a. Let I be an n-absorbing ideal of R. Is I a strongly n-absorbing ideal of R?

accepted.question_text: If I is an n-absorbing ideal of a ring R, must rad(I)^n be contained in I?

evidence.quote: Problem 30b. Let I be an n-absorbing ideal of R. Is rad(I)^n ⊆ I?

accepted.question_text: If I is an n-absorbing ideal of a ring R, must the extended ideal I[X] be n-absorbing in the polynomial ring R[X]?

evidence.quote: Problem 30c. Let I be an n-absorbing ideal of R. Is I[X] an n-absorbing ideal of the polynomial ring R[X]?

accepted.question_text: Develop a theory of projective star operations for projective varieties, that is, for finitely generated field extensions F/K that need not be purely transcendental, extending the theory already worked out for projective n-space.

evidence.quote: Develop projective star operations for projective varieties (i.e., for the case where F/K is a finitely generated field extension that need not be purely transcendental).

accepted.question_text: Is every stable Archimedean domain one-dimensional?

evidence.quote: Problem 32a. Is a stable Archimedean domain one-dimensional?

accepted.question_text: Let D be a one-dimensional Mori domain such that each divisorial ideal is 2-v-generated. Must every divisorial ideal of D be stable?

evidence.quote: Problem 32b. Let D be a one-dimensional Mori domain such that each divisorial ideal is 2-v-generated. Is it true that each divisorial ideal is stable?

accepted.question_text: Let D be a Mori domain such that each divisorial ideal is 2-v-generated. Must D be v-stable?

evidence.quote: Problem 32c. Let D be a Mori domain such that each divisorial ideal is 2-v-generated. Is it true that D is v-stable?

accepted.question_text: Assume D is a finitely stable LPI-domain, meaning every locally principal nonzero ideal is invertible. Must D have finite character?
accepted.context_brief: Finite character in finitely stable LPI-domains

evidence.quote: Assume that D is a finitely stable LPI-domain. Is it true that D has finite character?

accepted.question_text: For R = D + X D_S[X], find necessary and sufficient conditions for R to be a v-domain. In particular, prove or disprove that this holds exactly when D is a v-domain and the ideal (d, X) is v-invertible for every nonzero d in D.
accepted.context_brief: v-domains of D + X D_S[X] type

evidence.quote: Problem 34a. Find necessary and sufficient conditions for R = D + X D_S[X] to be a v-domain. Prove or disprove that R is a v-domain if and only if D is a v-domain and (d, X) is v-invertible for all d in D\{0}.

accepted.question_text: Let A ⊆ B be an extension of integral domains and X an indeterminate over B. Find necessary and sufficient conditions for the integral domain A + X B[X] to be a v-domain.

evidence.quote: Problem 34b. Let A ⊆ B be an extension of integral domains, and let X be an indeterminate over B. Find necessary and sufficient conditions for the integral domain A + XB[X] to be a v-domain.

accepted.question_text: Let D be an almost GCD domain such that every nonzero t-locally principal ideal is t-invertible. Must D have finite t-character?
accepted.context_brief: Finite t-character in almost GCD domains

evidence.quote: Let D be an almost GCD domain such that every nonzero t-locally principal ideal is t-invertible. Is D of finite t-character?

accepted.question_text: Let T be a nonempty collection of overrings of an integral domain D, and for each T in that collection let *_T be a semistar operation on T. Find conditions on the family T and on the semistar operations *_T under which the induced semistar operation E ↦ intersection of (ET)^{*_T} is of finite type on D.

evidence.quote: Problem 36a. Find conditions on T and on the semistar operations *_T under which the semistar operation induced on D by E ↦ intersection of (ET)^{*_T}, for E in F(D), is of finite type.

accepted.question_text: Let S be a nonempty collection of semistar operations on an integral domain D, and define the induced semistar operation by E ↦ intersection of E^* over * in S. Find conditions on S ensuring that this induced semistar operation is of finite type.

evidence.quote: Problem 36b. Let S be any non-empty collection of semistar operations on D and let ^S be the semistar operation defined by E^S := intersection of E^* for * in S, for all E in F(D). Find conditions on the set S for the semistar operation ^S on D to be of finite type.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a Krull domain, or even a factorial domain, whose polynomial ring has dimension strictly larger than 1 + dim(D), so that D fails to be a Jaffard domain?
accepted.context_brief: Bouvier conjecture for Krull or factorial domains

evidence.quote: Problem 37a. Is there a Krull (or, more particularly, factorial) domain D such that 1 + dim(D) < dim(D[X])?

accepted.question_text: For the specific three-dimensional factorial domain J described in the source as an ascending union of polynomial rings, is J locally Jaffard?
accepted.context_brief: Local Jaffard property of David’s example

evidence.quote: Problem 37b. Is J a locally Jaffard domain?

accepted.question_text: Let A ⊆ D be an extension of integral domains, where A is Noetherian and D is a subalgebra of an affine domain T over A. Must D be a locally Jaffard domain?
accepted.context_brief: Local Jaffard property of subalgebras of affine domains

evidence.quote: Problem 37c. Let A ⊆ D be an extension of integral domains, where A is Noetherian domain and D is a subalgebra of an affine domain T over A. Is D a locally Jaffard domain?

accepted.question_text: If R is a one-dimensional local Mori domain, is R locally tame in the factorization-theoretic sense defined in the source?

evidence.quote: Let R be a one-dimensional local Mori domain. Is R locally tame?

accepted.question_text: Analyze and describe non-unique factorization in Int(D) when D is a discrete valuation ring with finite residue field.

evidence.quote: Problem 39. Analyze and describe non-unique factorization in Int(D), where D is a DVR with finite residue field.

accepted.question_text: Find axioms that characterize the poset Spec(Q[x,y]).

evidence.quote: Problem 40a. Find axioms characterizing the poset Q[x,y].

accepted.question_text: Are the prime spectra Spec(Q[x,y]) and Spec(Q(sqrt(2))[x,y]) order-isomorphic as posets?
accepted.context_brief: Order-isomorphism of spectra over number fields

evidence.quote: Problem 40b. Are Spec(Q[x,y]) and Spec(Q(sqrt(2))[x,y]) order-isomorphic?

accepted.question_text: More generally, if F and K are algebraic number fields and A is a two-dimensional affine domain over F, is Spec(A) order-isomorphic to Spec(K[x,y])?
accepted.context_brief: Spectra of affine surfaces over number fields

evidence.quote: Problem 40c. More generally, let F and K be algebraic number fields. If A is a two-dimensional affine domain over F, is Spec(A) order-isomorphic to Spec(K[x,y])?

evidence.quote: Problem 40d. If Spec(F[x,y]) and Spec(K[x,y]) are order-isomorphic, are F and K necessarily isomorphic fields?

accepted.question_text: Let I be the integral closure of the monomial ideal (x^a, y^b, z^c) in a polynomial ring in three variables over a field. Classify all triples (a,b,c) for which every power of I is integrally closed.

evidence.quote: Problem 41. Classify all triples (a,b,c) for which all powers of I are integrally closed.

accepted.question_text: Is there a more direct algorithm for computing the integral closure of a general ideal, without first computing the integral closure of the entire Rees algebra?
accepted.context_brief: Algorithms for integral closure of ideals

evidence.quote: Problem 42a. Is there a more direct algorithm for computing the integral closure of a general ideal?

accepted.context_brief: Adapting algorithms for ideal integral closure

evidence.quote: Problem 42b. Can the Leonard-Pelikaan and Singh-Swanson algorithms be modified for computing the integral closure of ideals?

accepted.question_text: In the general Lipman-Sathaye theorem stated in the source, determine how tight the hypotheses are by relaxing individual assumptions and then either proving the resulting theorem or producing counterexamples to the relaxed versions.

evidence.quote: The suggested problem is to find how tight is the statement of this theorem: relax some assumption and either prove the theorem or find a counterexample for that relaxation.

accepted.question_text: Construct a Noetherian, two-dimensional, complete, integrally closed local domain (R,m) in which every m-primary ideal has more than one Rees valuation.

evidence.quote: Cutkosky proved the existence of a Noetherian, two-dimensional, complete, integrally closed local domain (R,m) in which every m-primary ideal has more than one Rees valuation. Give a construction of such a ring.
